This site distills the agnostic line of inquiry I follow. The long-form content has playbooks, write-ups, and projects I learn from. There's also a mosaic of thoughts I collect along the way An agnostic inquiry into systems, featuring long-form content and a shifting mosaic of thoughts.

The Horsepower Trap

Powerful engines pull rusted wagons, but they don't fix the rust. Fast hardware masks design noise. The resulting friction drains human time. A clear "why" makes systems adaptable.

×

A system that meets user needs can be complete but terminal. Isolate the common factors to carve a neutral core; it is the difference between a one-off tool and a scalable, reusable service.

×

Observability is not dashboards. It is the ability to ask new questions of your system without shipping new code. Systems that cannot be interrogated evolve blindly, guided more by superstition than evidence.

×

Users experience delay as uncertainty. Even when throughput is acceptable, long-tail latency erodes trust and amplifies perceived instability.

Latency is a product feature

Performance is not an implementation detail. It is part of the user contract, shaping how reliable and predictable a system feels under real conditions.

×
×

Design for recovery, not perfection

Improving performance in isolation often shifts complexity elsewhere. Always reason about the system boundary where incentives diverge.

×

Human workflows are part of the system

Alert fatigue, handoffs, and institutional knowledge gaps shape behavior as much as code paths do. Ignoring them creates invisible failure modes.

What you measure becomes what the system optimizes for, even when the metric stops representing the underlying goal.

×

Growth does not introduce new problems so much as it magnifies the ones that were quietly tolerated before. Scale is a stress test for assumptions, not a feature milestone.

Scale exposes assumptions.
